# Headlines: news (NEWS)

The headlines for one name, as the news connector computed them: newest first, filtered for relevance, duplicates removed. One row per headlines, keyed by NEWS_ID. Read by the **news-and-markets** pack's connector `news-store`. A **snapshot of public data**, captured 2026-10-18T03:24:33Z from Google News (news connector), refreshed whole by its script (External data); 71 records. A refresh replaces the whole snapshot.

## File layout

|  |  |
|---|---|
| Path | `data/testdata/news-and-markets/news/` + `snapshot-YYYY-MM-DD.jsonl.gz` |
| Format | JSON Lines: UTF-8, one JSON object a line, gzip-compressed (`.jsonl.gz`) |
| Key field | `NEWS_ID` |
| Date field | none in the record: a snapshot of public data, its file named by the capture date; the demo lake serves the same records on every business date (partition `business_date`) |
| Promoted columns | none (the whole record is kept as `doc`) |
| Vector fields | none |
| Partitioned by | `business_date` |
| A day's file | the whole snapshot |

## Field reference

Every field of the record above, nested ones as dotted paths (`[]` marks an array of objects). *Required* is the contract's; *in N%* is how often the test data fills it.

| Field | Type | Required | Meaning | Values, format, unit | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `NEWS_ID` | string | required | The record's id (the business key) | pattern `^NEWS-`; links to `news` | `"NEWS-Alphabet"` |
| `ENTITY` | string | required | The company or topic the headlines are about, as searched (Alphabet, Federal Reserve). | — | `"Alphabet"` |
| `ALIASES` | array of strings | required | Other names of the entity; a headline must name the entity or one of these to pass the relevance step. | — | [2 values] |
| `EDITION` | string | required | The Google News edition the headlines come from: language and country (en-US, de-DE, ja-JP). | one of `de-DE`, `en-US`, `ja-JP` | `"en-US"` |
| `RELEVANCE_FILTER` | string | required | on when headlines not about ENTITY were dropped (the pipeline's relevance step), off for the ~all record. | one of `off`, `on` | `"on"` |
| `COUNT` | integer | required | How many headlines ITEMS holds: at most the news connector's max-items setting (15 in the snapshot). | — | `15` |
| `FETCHED_AT` | string | required | When the headlines were fetched, as text: date and time in UTC, and in the snapshot "(snapshot captured <date>)". | one of `2026-10-18 03:25 UTC (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)`, `2026-10-18 03:26 UTC (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)`, `2026-10-18 03:27 UTC (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)` | `"2026-10-18 03:25 UTC (snapshot captured 2026-10-18)"` |
| `ITEMS` | array of objects | required | The headlines, newest first, one element each: PUBLISHED, SOURCE (the publisher), TITLE and LINK. | — | [15 objects] |
| `ITEMS[].PUBLISHED` | string | required | When the headline was published, as text (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC). | — | `"2026-10-18 01:37 UTC"` |
| `ITEMS[].SOURCE` | string | required | The publisher of the headline. | — | `"Simply Wall Street"` |
| `ITEMS[].TITLE` | string | required | The headline as the publisher wrote it. | — | `"Alphabet (GOOGL) Plans Toronto Robotaxi Service By 2028"` |
| `ITEMS[].LINK` | string | required | The link to the article (a Google News redirect URL). | — | `"https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiugFBVV95cUxOWF9ZU…` |
| `BY_SOURCE` | array of objects | required | How many of the headlines each publisher wrote, one element per publisher: SOURCE and COUNT. | — | [12 objects] |
| `BY_SOURCE[].SOURCE` | string | required | A publisher among ITEMS. | — | `"The Motley Fool"` |
| `BY_SOURCE[].COUNT` | integer | required | How many of ITEMS that publisher has. | — | `3` |
| `PIPELINE` | array of objects | required | What each step of the news pipeline did, one element per step in order (relevance, duplicates …): STEP, KEPT and DROPPED (headline counts). | — | [3 objects] |
| `PIPELINE[].DROPPED` | integer | required | How many headlines the step removed. | — | `4` |
| `PIPELINE[].KEPT` | integer | required | How many headlines remained after the step. | — | `96` |
| `PIPELINE[].STEP` | string | required | The pipeline step, in order: relevance (the title names the entity or an alias), duplicates (the same story or headline from the same publisher kept once, the newest), limit (at most the connector's max-items); sources (deny or allow lists) when set. | one of `duplicates`, `limit`, `relevance` | `"relevance"` |
| `FETCHED` | integer | required | How many headlines the feed returned before the pipeline (relevance, duplicates, limit) filtered them. | seen: `100`, `102`, `104`, `101`, `103`, `106`, `92` | `100` |
| `PROVENANCE` | object | required | Where the headlines come from, one object: FEED (Google News RSS), FETCHED, CACHED_FOR, TERMS and SNAPSHOT. | — | {…} |
| `PROVENANCE.FEED` | string | required | The feed the headlines came from (Google News RSS). | — | `"Google News RSS (news.google.com)"` |
| `PROVENANCE.FETCHED` | string | required | When the connector fetched the feed, as text (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC). | one of `2026-10-18 03:25 UTC`, `2026-10-18 03:26 UTC`, `2026-10-18 03:27 UTC` | `"2026-10-18 03:25 UTC"` |
| `PROVENANCE.CACHED_FOR` | string | required | How long the connector caches a fetch (its cache TTL), as text. | — | `"3600 s"` |
| `PROVENANCE.TERMS` | string | required | The terms the headlines may be shown under. | — | `"Headlines and links belong to their publishers; shown for …` |
| `PROVENANCE.SNAPSHOT` | string | required | Says the document is served from the committed snapshot in the demo lake, not live. | — | `"Snapshot captured 2026-10-18 03:24 UTC from Google News; s…` |
| `SNAPSHOT` | string | required | Says the document is a committed snapshot: when it was captured and from where (tools/testdata/capture_market.py). | — | `"Snapshot captured 2026-10-18 03:24 UTC from Google News"` |
| `SNAPSHOT_CAPTURED_AT` | timestamp (ISO-8601) | required | When the snapshot was captured, ISO-8601 UTC. | — | `"2026-10-18T03:24:33Z"` |

## For the production query

- **Identity:** one record per `NEWS_ID` per `snapshot`; the key is text, unique within the date.
- **Never null:** `NEWS_ID`, `ENTITY`, `ALIASES`, `EDITION`, `RELEVANCE_FILTER`, `COUNT`, `FETCHED_AT`, `ITEMS`, `BY_SOURCE`, `PIPELINE`, `FETCHED`, `PROVENANCE`, `SNAPSHOT`, `SNAPSHOT_CAPTURED_AT` (the contract's required fields).
- **Format:** JSON Lines, UTF-8, one object a line, gzip; field names exactly as shown (UPPER_SNAKE); dates `YYYY-MM-DD`; numbers as JSON numbers, never strings; a missing value is `null` or absent (an empty string is read as empty).
- **Arrays:** keep the order shown (vectors in the scenario set's or the run's order); nested objects as JSON, never flattened.
- Unique: `NEWS_ID` per snapshot.
- `NEWS_ID` matches `^NEWS-`.
- `COUNT` is at least 0.
- `BY_SOURCE[].COUNT` is at least 0.
